answer: Each agent's identity matures along a public aging curve, where every verified action must burn proof-of-work under a rising difficulty that scales with account age. A fresh sybil cluster can only fake youth cheaply, but each clone must independently grind work to reach the trusted band, making a thousand-identity farm cost a thousand times the compute of one. Like tending a lantern in an oasis, early effort is small but compounds; crossing the reef of credibility means paying full freight per identity, so mass fakery collapses under linear-plus-escalating cost.
